faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be in the Township of Langley?
faq.a: Zoning Bylaw s.102, as amended, caps a Township secondary suite at 120 m² with no percentage cap; note the documented conflict — the Township's January 2025 guide says suites are not permitted in townhouses/rowhouses, while the July 2025 s.102 definition says they may be (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/rules-gaps-2026-11-01.md, read 2026-11-01)

faq.q: Can an ALR property's additional residence sit over a garage?
faq.a: Yes, on the ALC's carriage-house exception: the garage below is excluded from the additional residence's floor area if it is one storey and for the principal residence's vehicles, does not exceed the additional residence's maximum floor area (90 m² or 186 m²), has no internal connection to the residence, and the residence is clustered close to the principal residence

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Langley?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Langley?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
